Subject: Request: Structured Early-Exit & Recovery Path for BlueOak POC

Team — looping you in for an executive exception request. BlueOak (RBW-3491) is asking for non-standard early-exit language tied to a phased downsell and a short recovery window. Quick summary and ask below: 

Summary:
- Customer: BlueOak Systems (pilot: 3 months, production target Q4)
- Current ask: ability to opt out of the committed ramp at month 2 with a 60-day notice, returning to a reduced committed level rather than full termination.
- Request drivers: unexpected budget reallocation + approval delays on their side. They want a structured escape that preserves runway for both sides.

Proposed carve (attached): recovery_schedule_v3.xlsx (links to proposed staged ramp-down and recovery credits)
- Month 1: full pilot commitment (baseline)
- Month 2: optional opt-out window with 60-day notice; if exercised, preserves 50% of committed capacity for next 90 days at 70% of committed rate (downsell protection)
- If customer re-ups within 180 days, we restore prior commit without a new onboarding fee; otherwise, the contract converts to standard metered terms
- Early-exit fee: one-time 10% of remaining committed ARR or a capped credit (whichever is lower) to offset operational scheduling costs

Why this is reasonable: keeps predictable utilization for Dedicated pools, gives BlueOak commercial flexibility, and limits churn/fingerprint risk. We propose an exec sign-off to make this an exception for this account only (precedent flagged).

Ask: executive approval for the exception + approval to offer a 10% one-time early-exit fee + permission for Sales to sign a mutual action plan with the attached redlines.

Attachments: BlueOak_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf, recovery_schedule_v3.xlsx, redlines_blueoak.docx

Next steps I propose:
- Aditya: confirm legal & revenue consistency with one-time fee and the recovery restore clause
- Monica: confirm ops impact on Dedicated pool scheduling and whether we can lock capacity for 90 days at reduced rate
- Marissa: executive OK to proceed with this template for BlueOak only (if yes, I'll present to procurement for signature)

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan — quick read. Two technical/legal clarifications before I can greenlight: 
1) The 10% early-exit fee calculation needs a cap in dollars and an explicit treatment for any pre-paid credits. If BlueOak paid in advance, we should net those against the fee.
2) The restoration clause (restore previous commit if re-up within 180 days) needs a guardrail: limit to the same region and model family (so they don't restore a heavier GPU footprint that impacts capacity planning).

If we add those guardrails, legal is fine with the commercial language; I’ll coordinate with Revenue Ops on revenue recognition for the one-time fee.

-Aditya

Thanks Aditya — incorporated those guardrails in the attached redlines (redlines_blueoak.docx). TL;DR of edits: 
- Early-exit fee: 10% of remaining committed ARR, capped at $45,000; pre-paid credits netted against fee.
- Restore clause: restore only to prior capacity within the same region/model family; any restoration that expands GPU tier requires re-approval.
- Added a 30-day blackout after opt-out during which the customer cannot flip-flop (to avoid churn gaming).

Monica — can ops commit to reserving 50% capacity at a reduced rate for 90 days if the opt-out is exercised? If there's an ops cost that would exceed our cap, flag it and we'll propose a different cap.

If all green, can Marissa sign for Sales exec approval? BlueOak is time-sensitive — they want to finalize by end of week.

-Jordan
